On that basis the lesson is fully coherent with what it claims to be: a 90-minute beginner skill-builder with a single narrow, achievable outcome, and it does not overclaim role readiness or certification value. It earns a mid score rather than high because even an optional resource benefits from a declared upward link — no mapping to a data-literacy competency, no role tags indicating who would benefit, and no stated relationship to adjacent Excel offerings, so a learner or manager cannot see where this sits in a skills progression.

severity_flags: CRITICAL — Surprise assessment: the 40%-weighted final requires interviewing, transcription, Braun & Clarke thematic coding, and theme development, none of which were practiced; the artifact explicitly confirms 'no coding practice, no transcript analysis exercise, no inter-rater reliability work.' This is a validity failure, not a rigor feature: scores will measure prior qualitative exposure rather than learning from this course.

CRITICAL — Zero assessment of 11 weeks of instruction: quantitative design, inferential statistics, SPSS, Likert construction, sampling theory, and APA reporting carry 0% of the final's weight, leaving ~92% of contact time unmeasured and signaling to learners that the taught content did not matter.

CRITICAL — Cognitive-level chasm: the qualitative content is taught at Remember/Understand (DoK 1 definitions plus one example in 90 minutes) and assessed at Create/Extended Thinking (DoK 4 independent fieldwork and interpretive analysis), skipping Apply and Analyze entirely.

HIGH — Rubric criteria untraceable to instruction: 'Coding rigor' (25%) and 'use of qualitative literature' (20%) assess a procedure never modeled and a literature base never assigned, so 45% of the grade rests on uninstructed content.

HIGH — Human-subjects execution with no preparation: the final requires recruiting and interviewing three live participants with no instruction in interview protocol design, consent/IRB process, or interviewing technique — an ethical as well as instructional exposure.

HIGH — Objective's 'appropriate to a stated research question' clause is neither taught nor assessed: no paradigm-comparison or method-selection work appears in instruction, and the assessment pre-specifies the method, so the objective's core judgment element is unmeasured.
MODERATE — No stated criterion in the objective and no linkage to any external competency framework, leaving rubric weights unjustified and the course unanchored to program or disciplinary outcomes.

rationale.objective_strategy_coherence: The objective says 'design and execute a research study appropriate to a stated research question, using sound methodology' — paradigm-neutral language that implies the learner can select among methodologies to fit a question. Instruction delivers only one half of that space: 11 of 12 weeks are exclusively quantitative (designs, SPSS, survey/sampling, APA tables). The Create-level verbs ('design and execute') are partially practiced quantitatively, but 'appropriate to a stated research question' — the Evaluate-level judgment of matching method to question — is never taught, because no paradigm comparison or method-selection decision work appears anywhere. The Week 12 qualitative lecture is pure Remember/Understand (definitions, one example, no practice), well below the Create level the objective states. Score is 2 rather than 1 because the quantitative instruction is internally purposeful and does trace to the 'design and execute... sound methodology' portion of the objective.
rationale.strategy_assessment_coherence: This is the most severe break. The assessment demands skills that received zero practice: conducting interviews, transcribing, coding transcripts, developing themes, and writing findings with quoted excerpts. The artifact states explicitly: 'no coding practice, no transcript analysis exercise, no inter-rater reliability work.' The single 90-minute Week 12 lecture mentioned thematic analysis definitionally and showed one example; the assessment asks learners to execute Braun & Clarke (2006) coding independently — a jump from Remember (DoK 1) to Create/Extended Thinking (DoK 4) with nothing in between. Meanwhile the entire taught skillset (SPSS, t-tests/ANOVA/regression, Likert construction, sampling, APA tables) is assessed at 0%. Format mismatch is total as well: practice was software-driven numeric analysis, assessment is human-subject fieldwork plus interpretive writing. The rubric compounds it — 'use of qualitative literature' (20%) tests a literature base never assigned, and 'coding rigor' (25%) tests a procedure never modeled with feedback. This is a textbook surprise assessment; it scores 1.
rationale.objective_assessment_coherence: Scored on its own terms, the assessment is not disconnected from the objective's verbs — 'design and execute a research study' is literally what the qualitative report asks for, at the matching Create/DoK 4 level, and the rubric's coding-rigor and theme-development criteria are plausible operationalizations of 'sound methodology.' What breaks the match is the 'appropriate to a stated research question' clause: the assessment pre-specifies the method (thematic analysis, 3 interviews) rather than requiring the learner to justify methodological fit, so the objective's selection/appropriateness criterion is never measured. The objective also contains no criterion statement, so the rubric's four weights (25/25/20/30) are not traceable to any stated standard — the criterion in the objective is not the criterion in the rubric because the objective states none. Score 2; this triggers the overall cap at 3.0, though the mean already falls below it.
rationale.coverage_completeness: Orphans run in both directions and are near-total. Orphan instruction: weeks 1-11 — quantitative design, inferential statistics, SPSS, survey construction, sampling theory, APA tables — constitute roughly 92% of contact time and are assessed at 0% in the 40%-weighted final. Orphan assessment: interviewing, transcription, coding, theme development, and qualitative literature appear in the rubric (100% of its weight) with essentially no instructional antecedent. No blueprint or table of specifications is present or derivable: a two-way chart of objectives × instruction × assessment items would show a single objective, an 11-week instructional block mapping to nothing assessed, and a rubric mapping to nothing taught. Under Dick & Carey (2015) and Wiggins & McTighe (2005) backward-design logic, the assessment was evidently selected independently of both the objective decomposition and the instructional plan. Score 1.
rationale.vertical_alignment: Within the quantitative strand, weeks 1-11 show genuine and defensible progression: designs (1-3) precede analysis (4-6), which precedes instrument construction and sampling (7-9), which precedes reporting (10-11) — prerequisites are respected and later content extends rather than repeats earlier content, consistent with elaboration logic (Reigeluth 1999). That strand alone would score 4. The failure is at the transition: Week 12 introduces an entirely new paradigm as a terminal 90-minute add-on with no prerequisite scaffolding, no spiral return, and no whole-task progression toward the qualitative performance the final demands (van Merriënboer & Kirschner 2018 would require part-task coding practice and faded guidance across several weeks). The course effectively ends one unit before the skill it certifies, so the overall vertical logic is reverse-coherent — the capstone sits atop a staircase built for a different building. Score 2, reflecting the strong strand offset by a terminal discontinuity.
rationale.discipline_alignment: No external competency framework, accreditation standard, or program-level outcome is cited anywhere, so there is no stated upward linkage from the course objective to a discipline competency. This is a graduate education research-methods course, a context where such linkage is normally expected (e.g., CAEP/AERA research-preparation standards or program-level research competencies), so the omission is a genuine gap rather than an adaptation for a non-disciplinary artifact. Partial credit is warranted because the content and the rubric both invoke real disciplinary anchors — Braun & Clarke (2006) for thematic analysis, APA reporting conventions — indicating implicit awareness of a professional knowledge base, and a graduate methods course plausibly serves a thesis/dissertation requirement. But no objective maps upward to any named competency (Hirumi, Ratliff & de la Mora 2021; Hirumi 2025, Fig. 1), and the paradigm imbalance means the course cannot claim to prepare a methodologically complete researcher under any framework. Score 2.
rationale.note_on_scoring: Mean of six dimensions = (2+1+2+1+2+2)/6 = 1.67. The 3.0 cap triggered by objective_assessment_coherence = 2 is not binding here.

severity_flags: Week 5 'React State Management' exhibits two-level Bloom collapse across all three components: Apply objective → Understand instruction → Remember assessment. Learners can earn credit for the module without ever demonstrating the stated behavior, and the misalignment compounds in a single direction rather than canceling.

Week 11 'Database Normalization' assesses an Analyze-level skill that was never practiced — instruction supplies worked examples only. This is a learner-surprise condition: the assessment is a first encounter with the performance, not a measure of a rehearsed one.

Program-level strengths (vertical and discipline alignment) are documented at the curriculum map level while unit-level coherence is failing. Strong macro-alignment is masking micro-misalignment, which is the harder failure mode to detect in review — a graduate can complete a coherently sequenced program and still arrive at the capstone without the component skills its objectives promised.

Only 3 of approximately 36+ modules are documented. The two-of-three failure rate in the visible sample is a significant risk signal for the undocumented remainder and should not be treated as the full extent of the problem.

rationale.objective_strategy_coherence: Two of the three documented unit modules show instruction operating below the stated objective's Bloom level. Week 5 'React State Management' states an Apply objective ('Apply React hooks to manage component state in a real application') but delivers 80% lecture and reading with a single small in-class exercise — Understand-level instruction supporting an Apply-level objective. Week 11 'Database Normalization' states an Analyze objective ('Analyze schemas and identify normalization violations') but instruction provides worked examples only, with no analysis practice — learners never perform the objective verb before being held to it. Week 8 'REST API Design' is the lone module where instruction genuinely teaches the stated Apply behavior. Pattern suggests a design habit of under-powering instruction relative to objective verbs, not isolated slips.
rationale.strategy_assessment_coherence: Both flagged modules break this pair in opposite directions, so neither can be excused as an instruction-assessment pair that merely missed the objective. Week 5: instruction reaches Understand (lecture/reading plus one exercise) while assessment drops to Remember (multiple-choice on hook syntax) — the assessment tests recall of syntax that practice did not emphasize and ignores the one hands-on exercise entirely. Week 11 is the more serious transactional-distance failure: assessment demands schema analysis that was never practiced, only modeled through examples. This is a learner surprise in the strict sense — a tested skill that was mentioned and demonstrated but not rehearsed. Week 8 alone shows practice and assessment matched in format and cognitive demand.
rationale.objective_assessment_coherence: Mixed, and the two flagged modules diverge sharply. Week 11 is a clean verb-to-task match: an Analyze objective paired with an analysis task, so the objective-assessment contract holds even though instruction fails to support it. Week 8 matches at Apply. Week 5 is a two-level Bloom drop — an Apply objective ('manage component state in a real application', DoK 2-3, performance-based) assessed by a multiple-choice syntax quiz (Remember, DoK 1). No criterion from the objective ('in a real application') appears in the assessment at all; a learner could pass the quiz without ever writing a functioning stateful component. One of three documented modules in clear violation, two in alignment, places this at the midpoint rather than in the capped band.
rationale.coverage_completeness: Every objective appears to be addressed in both instruction and assessment — no orphan objectives or orphan content are reported at the modules documented, and a blueprint is partially derivable since each module names an objective, an instructional approach, and an assessment. Coverage is undermined on two counts: (1) the artifact documents only 3 modules across a 12-week program, so coverage claims for the remaining weeks are asserted rather than evidenced; (2) coverage at the Week 5 module is nominal rather than real — the objective is 'covered' by a quiz that measures a different cognitive level, which is coverage in the table-of-specifications sense only. A true table of specifications with Bloom level per cell would expose these as gaps rather than fills.
rationale.vertical_alignment: Strongest dimension and well-evidenced. The 12-week progression (fundamentals → React frontend → Node/Express backend → databases and integration → capstone) follows a defensible whole-task elaboration sequence: each phase explicitly builds on the previous, prerequisites are stated rather than assumed, and the capstone synthesizes all prior phases rather than repeating any one. This is consistent with 4C/ID whole-task progression (van Merriënboer & Kirschner 2018) and Reigeluth's elaboration logic — later content extends earlier content, and the full-stack integration phase (Weeks 10-11) is correctly placed after both frontend and backend competence rather than before. Prerequisite respect is real: React (Weeks 4-6) follows JavaScript fundamentals (Weeks 1-3); database work follows backend.
rationale.discipline_alignment: Explicit and traceable. Outcomes map to the bootcamp's published 'Junior Developer Readiness' competency framework, which is itself aligned to hiring partner job descriptions — a two-step upward linkage from unit objectives to program competencies to external labor-market criteria, satisfying the mapping expectation in Hirumi, Ratliff & de la Mora (2021). The framework is named and published rather than implied, and the external anchor (hiring partner job descriptions) is the appropriate discipline referent for a vocational bootcamp where no accrediting examination exists. Minor residual: the artifact does not show the per-objective crosswalk, so upward mapping is credible at the program level but not individually verified at the lesson level.
